CHART CODE
 import plotly.graph_objects as go
import pandas as pd

data = {
    "Region": [
        "Northeast Asia", "Northeast Asia", "Northeast Asia",
        "Southeast Asia", "Southeast Asia", "Southeast Asia",
        "Sub-Saharan Africa", "Sub-Saharan Africa", "Sub-Saharan Africa",
        "South Asia", "South Asia", "South Asia",
        "Latin America", "Latin America", "Latin America",
        "Eastern Europe", "Eastern Europe", "Eastern Europe",
        "Western Europe", "Western Europe", "Western Europe",
        "North America", "North America", "North America"
    ],
    "Performance Impact": [
        "Positive", "Neutral", "Negative",
        "Positive", "Neutral", "Negative",
        "Positive", "Neutral", "Negative",
        "Positive", "Neutral", "Negative",
        "Positive", "Neutral", "Negative",
        "Positive", "Neutral", "Negative",
        "Positive", "Neutral", "Negative",
        "Positive", "Neutral", "Negative"
    ],
    "Value": [
        220, 95, -180,
        200, 80, -150,
        140, 75, -120,
        195, 85, -145,
        170, 70, -110,
        230, 80, -90,
        240, 70, -80,
        250, 85, -101
    ],
    "Network Type": [
        "5G", "5G", "4G",
        "4G", "4G", "3G",
        "4G", "3G", "3G",
        "4G", "4G", "2G",
        "4G", "3G", "2G",
        "5G", "4G", "3G",
        "5G", "5G", "4G",
        "5G", "5G", "5G"
    ],
    "Operator Count": [
        12, 8, 5,
        10, 7, 4,
        8, 6, 3,
        9, 6, 3,
        7, 5, 2,
        11, 7, 2,
        13, 6, 1,
        14, 8, 1
    ]
}

df = pd.DataFrame(data)
df_pos = df[df["Performance Impact"] == "Positive"].sort_values(by="Value", ascending=False)
df_neg = df[df["Performance Impact"] == "Negative"].sort_values(by="Value", ascending=True)

fig = go.Figure()

fig.add_trace(go.Bar(
    y=df_pos["Region"],
    x=df_pos["Value"],
    name="Positive Impact",
    orientation="h",
    marker=dict(color="#1f77b4"),
    text=df_pos["Network Type"],
    textposition="inside",
    insidetextanchor="middle"
))

fig.add_trace(go.Bar(
    y=df_neg["Region"],
    x=df_neg["Value"],
    name="Negative Impact",
    orientation="h",
    marker=dict(color="#d62728"),
    text=df_neg["Network Type"],
    textposition="inside",
    insidetextanchor="middle"
))

fig.update_layout(
    title="Impact of Network Performance on Operator Growth by Region (2023)",
    xaxis_title="Net Growth in Operator Count (Positive/Negative)",
    yaxis_title="Region",
    barmode="relative",
    height=700,
    width=1000,
    margin=dict(l=150, r=50, t=80, b=50),
    plot_bgcolor="white",
    paper_bgcolor="white",
    legend=dict(orientation="h", yanchor="bottom", y=1.02, xanchor="right", x=1)
)

fig.update_xaxes(showgrid=True, gridwidth=1, gridcolor="#f0f0f0")
fig.update_yaxes(tickfont=dict(size=10))

fig.write_image("output.png")
SUMMARY
 The chart titled "Impact of Network Performance on Operator Growth by Region (2023)" is a tornado chart, which visually compares the positive and negative impacts of different network generations on operator growth across various regions. The horizontal bars extend both to the right and left from a central vertical axis, where the right side represents positive growth in operator count and the left side represents negative growth. The regions are listed along the vertical axis, from North America at the top to Sub-Saharan Africa at the bottom.

Each bar is color-coded, with blue indicating positive impacts and red indicating negative impacts. Within each bar, the specific network type (e.g., 2G, 3G, 4G, or 5G) is labeled directly on the bar to show which generation is contributing to the growth or decline. For instance, North America displays a positive impact exclusively from 5G, showing a net growth of 250 operators, while its negative impact is minimal, attributed to 5G with a negligible decline. Western Europe also shows strong positive growth from 5G with a net increase of 240 operators, whereas its negative impact, stemming from 4G, is relatively small at -80.

In Eastern Europe, the positive impact from 5G results in an increase of 230 operators, while 3G contributes to a negative impact of -90. Northeast Asia shows a positive influence from 5G, adding 220 operators, but a significant negative impact from 4G, reducing operator count by 180. Southeast Asia, South Asia, Latin America, and Sub-Saharan Africa similarly display a mix of positive and negative impacts from different network generations, with 4G predominantly driving positive growth in these regions while older generations like 2G and 3G are associated with negative impacts.

The chart effectively highlights the varying degrees of influence different network technologies have on operator growth across global regions, illustrating a clear trend where newer network generations generally contribute to positive growth, while older ones correlate with declines.
